text: Replace pointwise binary cross-entropy with a within-user listwise softmax loss on the existing additive-plus-16-dimensional user-video interaction model: for each training user having at least one long_view-positive and one negative impression, normalize scores across that user’s impressions and minimize the positive-label-weighted negative log likelihood, while retaining the same model parameters, optimizer settings, split, checkpointing, and fixed within-user evaluation. This tests whether directly concentrating probability mass on each user’s positives improves the primary metric and nDCG@5 without changing the scored output or introducing cross-user comparisons.
rationale: The referenced scored model reaches primary 0.5885, GAUC 0.6499, and nDCG@5 0.5272, while global AUC is higher at 0.7435, suggesting that row-level discrimination is not fully translating into within-user top-of-list quality. Its MAP@5 of 0.4743, MRR@5 of 0.5332, HitRate@5 of 0.6743, Precision@5 of 0.3718, and Recall@5 of 0.5931 indicate room to improve concentration of positives near the top. Classification diagnostics show recall 0.7729 versus precision 0.4571 and a predicted-positive rate of 0.5297 against prevalence 0.3133, reinforcing that pointwise training may overproduce positives. A grouped listwise objective directly targets relative allocation within each user, skips users without both classes, requires only bounded per-user softmax computations, and preserves the official primary objective plus all classification, ranking, and score-distribution diagnostics.
